PREFACE
The Fourth Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica completed all its
objectives, and the results of the scientific investigations largely carried out
during the year 1984-85, have been presented in this report. The first wintering
team which was left behind in Antarctica by the Third Expedition returned
with the Fourth Expedition. Another wintering team consisting of thirteen
members was left behind by the Fourth Expedition and all the members of this
team also returned in the end of March 1986, after completing their task.
The progress made by the successive Indian Expeditions to Antarctica, which
started in 1981-82, has been steady and satisfying. By 1985, India has not
only established a permanent station "Dakshin Gangotri", but also built ano-
ther small summer station "Maitri" consisting of three cottages in the Schirma-
cher Oasis, a hanger and an alternate emergency accommodation near the per-
manent station. In addition, we have also established a High Frequency (HF)
communication link between Dakshin Gangotri station and India.
The papers published on the Antarctic investigations by the Indian scien-
tists during the last few years, now amounting to nearly 200, clearly indicate
the growing interest in polar research in the country. At present, there are
nearly 25 institutions in India working on the data, material and samples col-
lected from Antarctica.
This Technical Report gives the details of the scientific work carried out
by the Indian scientists in the  disciplines of geology, geophysics, meteorology,
biology, oceanography, polymer chemistry, renewable energy systems etc. It is
greatly hoped that the Report of the Fourth Expedition will be as well received
by the Antarctic scientists throughout the world, as the earlier three reports.
December, 1987
S.Z. QASIM 
Secretary
